ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AB=6\,cm$, $BC=12\,cm$, $\angle B=90^\circ$. Point P starts from point A and moves towards point B along side $AB$ at a speed of $1\,cm/s$, and point Q starts from point B and moves towards point C along side $BC$ at a speed of $2\,cm/s$. If P and Q start moving from A and B at the same time, respectively, and the moving time is denoted as $t\,(s)$. At what value of $t$ is the area of $\triangle PBQ$ equal to $9\,cm^{2}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given the problem, point $P$ starts moving from point $A$ towards point $B$ along side $AB$ at a speed of $1\,cm/s$, and point $Q$ starts moving from point $B$ towards point $C$ along side $BC$ at a speed of $2\,cm/s$,\\
$\therefore AP=t$, $BQ=2t$,\\
$\therefore BP=AB-AP=6-t$;\\
Since the area of $\triangle PBQ$ is $9\,cm^{2}$,\\
$\therefore \frac{1}{2}\cdot 2t\cdot (6-t)=9$,\\
solving yields, $t=\boxed{3}$.\\
That is, when $t=3$, the area of $\triangle PBQ$ is $9\,cm^{2}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows triangle ABC with AB as the horizontal base and BC as the vertical side, meeting at B at a right angle. Point P is on segment AB between A and B, with an arrow indicating motion from A toward B. Point Q is on segment BC between B and C, with an arrow indicating motion upward from B toward C. Segment PQ is drawn, and PB and BQ are perpendicular legs of triangle PBQ. Reasoning: After t seconds, P has moved AP = 1*t = t cm, and Q has moved BQ = 2*t = 2t cm. Since AB = 6 cm, BP = AB - AP = 6 - t. Because PB is perpendicular to BQ, the area of triangle PBQ is (1/2)(BP)(BQ) = (1/2)(6 - t)(2t). Set this equal to 9: (1/2)(6 - t)(2t) = 9, so t(6 - t) = 9. This gives 6t - t^2 = 9, or t^2 - 6t + 9 = 0, hence (t - 3)^2 = 0. Therefore t = 3 seconds.
